reason: Children are a one-line list of the three temporary purposes and a one-line identification of the ultimate purpose as liberation; the following cited discussion concerns the purpose of homage as a whole.
Children give extended analyses of what the darkness is (two obscurations, four kinds of non-afflicted ignorance, with scripture) and how the Buddha destroyed it, answering objections.
Children explain ultimate and conventional Abhidharma at length, debating aggregates, realms and rival views of the schools.
Children refute another system, set out the own position with several masters' views, and answer objections.
Children explain the nature of the four purposes-and-connections, argue why they are exactly four, and analyse whether they are one or distinct, with objections and citations.
Children argue whether analytical cessations are one or many and resolve a conflict with scripture, presenting Vaibhasika and Sautrantika positions.
Children set out the four alternatives with critique and analyse the third alternative at length with objections and replies.
Two children discuss the number, arrangement and sequence of the eight chapters with differing masters' views; only the third is a one-line pointer.
Children discuss where objects and faculties exist, how objects and faculties produce consciousness, and which consciousness arises first, citing rival views and answering doubts.
Children give long analyses of non-revealing form (definition debates, mindless states, critiques) and of the four great elements with scriptural citations.
Children explain at length how aggregates, sense-bases and elements named in other sutras are subsumed, with school disagreements and sutra citations.
Each of the eight children discusses a classification of the eighteen elements in detail, with objections, rival views and citations.
Children explain at length how faculties are obtained at birth and abandoned at death, including the faculties needed to attain the fruits, with debate and citations.
Children discuss the definition of mental factors, their substantial versus imputed status across schools, their realms and levels, their accompanying consciousnesses and etymology, with citations.
